entries.topic: Emanuela Orlandi and Mirella Gregori: the disappearances, the 1983 calls and communiqués, the papal appeals

claims.text: Emanuela Orlandi, 15, lived in Vatican City and disappeared on 22 June 1983 after leaving for a music lesson in Rome; her father Ercole Orlandi worked for the Prefecture of the Papal Household and was a citizen of Vatican City State

Mirella Gregori, 15, disappeared in Rome on 7 May 1983, about 40 days before Orlandi; last seen after school near a bar below her family's apartment, having told her mother she would meet a friend named Alessandro; no Vatican connection; linked to Orlandi by 1983 calls claiming both girls

On 22 June 1983 Orlandi attended the music school at Piazza Sant'Apollinare, phoned home about an offer of 375,000 lire to distribute cosmetics publicity, and was last seen at a bus stop around 7:30 pm; her father, a clerk of the Prefecture of the Papal Household, reported her missing
3 July 1983: John Paul II at the Angelus prayed that Emanuela 'possa presto tornare incolume'
Callers 'Pierluigi' and 'Mario' contacted the family in late June 1983; from 5 July a caller with an anglophone accent ('l'Americano') claimed to hold her and asked for a direct line to the Vatican
19 July 1983: the Vatican confirmed it had installed a hot line requested by the presumed kidnappers; a tape demanded the release of Mehmet Ali Agca, jailed for shooting the pope in 1981

Communiqués from Aug 1983 to 1984 in the names of 'Turkesh' (Fronte Liberazione Turco Anti Cristiano), 'Phoenix', a 'new Muslim organisation' and the Grey Wolves demanded Agca's release; no proof they held Emanuela was ever provided
20 October 1983 President Sandro Pertini appealed for release; 24 December 1983 John Paul II visited the Orlandi home and called it a case of international terrorism

Gregori family lawyer Nicodemo Gentile (2025) holds the Gregori case is separate and local; focus on the bar on via Volturno and friend Sonia De Vito; Dec 2025 memos to the commission on an identikit and 16 minors missing in Rome May-June 1983

entries.topic: Orlandi theories graded: Agca/Grey Wolves, Magliana/De Pedis, Marcinkus/IOR, abuse theories, 2017 document, the uncle lead, John Paul II remarks

claims.text: Enrico De Pedis, of the Magliana gang, was shot dead in Campo de' Fiori on 2 February 1990 and buried in the crypt of Sant'Apollinare after a letter from the rector Mgr Piero Vergari calling him a benefactor; Cardinal Ugo Poletti signed the authorisation

2008: Sabrina Minardi, De Pedis's former girlfriend, said De Pedis carried out the abduction on the orders of Archbishop Paul Marcinkus, IOR head; the Vatican said the claim had 'extremely doubtful value'; Lombardi said defamatory accusations without basis were spread against a dead man

2005 an anonymous caller to a TV show said the answer lay in De Pedis's tomb; April 2012 the Vatican said it had no objection to opening it and Lombardi said the Holy See 'had done everything possible'
14 May 2012 forensic police opened the tomb: one male body; samples taken; about 200 containers of bones found in the nearby ossuary; no link to Orlandi found
Agca first said Bulgarian agents/Grey Wolves kidnapped her, later in prison that she was alive in a convent; his statements shifted
May 2012 exorcist Gabriele Amorth said she was a victim of clerical sexual exploitation; no evidence produced
Vatican Girl (Netflix, 2022) included a friend saying Emanuela told her a week before that a high-ranking Vatican cleric had made advances

September 2017: Emiliano Fittipaldi published (La Repubblica, from his book) an unsigned memo on plain paper attributed to Cardinal Lorenzo Antonetti (APSA) to Re and Tauran, listing about half a billion lire spent 1983-1997 incl. a London residence; Fittipaldi said he could not verify it; Greg Burke called it 'false and ridiculous'; Re denied seeing it; the Secretariat of State 'firmly denies' authenticity

11 April 2023 Pietro Orlandi met Diddi for eight hours, then on La7's DiMartedi played audio of an alleged mobster claiming John Paul II went out at night with monsignors; no evidence offered; Tornielli wrote 'Evidence? None. Clues? Least of all.'; Dziwisz called it false
16 April 2023 Francis at the Regina Caeli said John Paul II had been 'object of offensive and unfounded inferences'
Pietro Orlandi's lawyer Laura Sgro said he 'did not intend to make accusations against any person'

10 July 2023 TG La7 reported 1983 Casaroli correspondence with the family's Colombian confessor on advances by uncle Mario Meneguzzi (dead) toward Natalina Orlandi in 1978; Natalina called them verbal and ended; family says he was on holiday outside Rome; Pietro: 'The Vatican wants to offload responsibility on my family'; Vatican (Bruni, 12 July) said no violation of the seal of confession

entries.topic: Orlandi/Gregori investigations: Rome prosecutors to 2016, bones 2018-2019, Vatican 2023, Rome 2023, parliamentary commission 2023-2026

claims.text: 19 October 2015 GIP Giovanni Giorgianni archived the second investigation (Orlandi and Gregori) at the request of Pignatone, Maisto and Calo; six suspects incl. Vergari, Sergio Virtu, Angelo Cassani, Gianfranco Cerboni, Minardi, Marco Accetti; evidence lacked consistency; Accetti judged unreliable; the family's opposition rejected
By 6 May 2016 the Court of Cassation (sixth section) rejected the family's appeal; Pietro Orlandi said no power could stop the truth
The first investigation was dismissed in 1997; 2 April 2012 prosecutor Capaldo said the Vatican knew the truth and was replaced on the file by Pignatone
Bones found in late October 2018 at the Apostolic Nunciature (Villa Giorgina); announced 30 October; Rome prosecutors: male, carbon dating pre-1964, neither Orlandi nor Gregori

Promoter of Justice Gian Piero Milano ordered the opening on 27 June 2019 after a letter to the family ('Look where the angel is pointing'); 11 July 2019 tombs of Princess Sophie von Hohenlohe and Duchess Charlotte Frederica of Mecklenburg-Schwerin opened, both empty; Gisotti: 'no human remains or funerary urns were found'

Ossuaries examined from 20 July 2019; 28 July Holy See press office: several hundred partially intact bone structures and thousands of fragments, none later than end of the 19th century (Prof. Giovanni Arcudi); family requested lab tests on about 70 fragments; samples held by the Gendarmerie
9 January 2023 the Vatican said Promoter of Justice Alessandro Diddi opened a file in part 'on the requests made by the family'; Pietro called it a 'positive step'
Rome prosecutors reopened in May 2023 (prosecutor Stefano Luciani, carabinieri Nucleo Investigativo); the Vatican sent material to Rome about six months after January 2023
23 March 2023 the Chamber of Deputies approved the commission bill 245-0

June 2023 Diddi at a Senate hearing said a new commission would be 'un'intromissione perniciosa per la genuinita delle indagini'; Parolin's letter objected to the form of the summons; Pignatone asked for text changes

9 November 2023 Senate voted nearly unanimously; Legge 4 dicembre 2023 n. 202 (GU 22 December 2023, in force 6 January 2024) created a commission under Art. 82 Constitution with the powers and limits of the judicial authority, for the duration of the legislature; it must report to the Chambers
14 March 2024 the commission (40 members, both chambers) elected Senator Andrea De Priamo (FdI) president; Morassut and Marchetti vice-presidents
April 2024 Pietro Orlandi said the Vatican did not want the commission; June 2024 he called the Vatican inquiry a 'farce' saying witnesses he suggested had not been called
June 2024 De Priamo said the Foreign Ministry was helping obtain 1983 diplomatic correspondence and that it would dispel portrayals of the Vatican as 'il male assoluto'
21 November 2024 the commission heard Domenico Giani, who said he compiled a 2012 folder ('historical reconstruction') and 'I am not a witness to anything'; commission declined to hear Agca
Jan-Mar 2025 the commission found empty files at the Archivio Centrale dello Stato and asked the Interior Ministry to check
2 August 2025 Pietro Orlandi said Leo XIV had not mentioned Emanuela at the 22 June Angelus and no meeting had been arranged
December 2025 Rome prosecutors registered former music-school classmate Laura Casagrande as a suspect for false statements; registration does not imply involvement; uncle's home searched 2024

29 January 2026 (76th sitting) and 5 February 2026 (77th sitting) the commission heard Pino Nicotri, Dolores Brugnoli and Armando Palmegiani; commissioners said no objective confirmation of Nicotri's hypotheses
